h1: The 7 Best Wet-Dry Shop Vacuums for Garages, Job Sites and Spills, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 wet-dry shop vacuums from DEWALT, Stanley, Vacmaster, Amazon Basics and Craftsman compared on tank size, peak HP and filters.
summary: The DEWALT 9 gallon wet-dry vac with attachments is the shop vacuum to buy for heavy and frequent use, and the DEWALT DXV06P 6 gallon with a blower port is the better all-rounder for a garage. The Vacmaster 8 gallon with a self-cleaning filter suits dusty workshops, the Stanley 6 gallon is the budget workhorse, and the Craftsman 2.5 gallon is the compact choice.
intro: Peak horsepower is the loudest number on a shop vacuum box and the least useful. It is calculated at a moment when the motor is spinning with no load, a condition that never happens while you vacuum, so a 5 peak HP badge and a 3 HP badge can behave much alike. What actually separates one shop vac from another is tank size, hose diameter, the filter and how easy it is to empty and clean.

We reviewed eight wet-dry vacuums from their titles and specification lines, set aside the smallest model, and ranked seven. Most listings give only gallons and horsepower, so we point out missing details such as hose size and filter type instead of guessing. All are corded 120-volt machines, and price buckets replace exact prices. This ranking comes from research rather than product trials.

products.name: DEWALT 9 Gallon Wet/Dry VAC, Heavy-Duty Shop Vacuum with Attachments, 5 Peak HP
products.verdict: A 9 gallon heavy-duty vac with attachments and 5 peak HP, built for contractors and frequent use.
products.description:
DEWALT's 9 gallon wet-dry vacuum is billed as heavy duty, comes with attachments and carries a 5 peak HP rating. It is the most expensive model here, in the $100 to $200 range.

The nine-gallon tank is the reason to choose it. A bigger drum means fewer trips to empty it, which matters when you clear drywall dust, wood chips or a flooded basement. The attachments make it usable for more than floors, such as corners, upholstery and tight spaces. It ranks first because tank volume and build matter more than a horsepower claim. The weight and size make it harder to store than the smaller units.

Buy it if you run a workshop, a job site or a big garage. Skip it if you want something easy to tuck into a closet.
products.skipIf: You have a small closet for storage.

products.name: DEWALT Shop Vacuum 6 Gal 4 HP Poly Wet/Dry Vacuum with Blower DXV06P
products.verdict: A 6 gallon poly-tank vac with 4 peak HP and a blower function for clearing leaves and debris.
products.description:
The DXV06P is a six gallon wet-dry vacuum with a poly tank, a 4 HP rating and a blower function, priced between $50 and $100.

A blower port turns the exhaust into a leaf and dust blower, which is a real convenience for clearing a garage floor, a deck or a car interior. A poly tank is dent resistant and light, though it is less rigid than steel. At six gallons it is large enough for most homes without being a burden to move. It ranks second because the capacity is smaller than the nine gallon, but the price is much lower.

Buy it if you want one shop vac for the garage, the car and the deck. Skip it if you will fill a bigger drum every day.
cons: Poly is less rigid than steel
products.skipIf: You need a very large tank.

products.name: Vacmaster Professional VDK811PW 0201 8 Gal Wet/Dry Vac Self-Cleaning Filter
products.verdict: An 8 gallon professional-line vacuum with a self-cleaning filter for fine dust.
products.description:
The Vacmaster VDK811PW is an eight gallon wet-dry vacuum from the Professional line, listed with a self-cleaning filter and priced between $50 and $100.

The self-cleaning filter is the standout, because fine dust clogs a standard filter quickly and wrecks suction. A mechanism that shakes or flicks the filter clean keeps performance up during a long sanding or drywall job. Eight gallons is generous, and the price is lower than the DEWALT. It ranks third because the listing gives no horsepower or hose details, and Vacmaster is a lesser-known name than DEWALT.

Buy it if you create fine dust in a workshop. Check the hose diameter and filter type with the seller.

products.name: Stanley - SL18116P Wet/Dry Vacuum, 6 Gallon, 4 Horsepower Black
products.verdict: A 6 gallon, 4 HP vac at the lowest price for its size, in the $25 to $50 range.
products.description:
The Stanley SL18116P is a six gallon wet-dry vacuum rated at 4 HP, and it costs between $25 and $50.

It is the value pick in a category where most people overpay for horsepower badges. Six gallons covers a garage, a basement or a car, and the price is the lowest for that size. It ranks fourth because it lacks a blower function or a self-cleaning filter, and the build is more basic than the DEWALT models. The listing is also short on attachments and hose details.

Buy it if you want a capable, cheap shop vac for occasional work. Skip it if you need heavy-duty construction.

products.name: DEWALT DXV04T 4 Gallon 5 Peak HP Portable Corded Wet/Dry Shop Vacuum
products.verdict: A 4 gallon portable DEWALT with 5 peak HP, made for job sites and big cleanups.
products.description:
The DXV04T is a four gallon corded portable wet-dry vacuum with a 5 peak HP rating, priced between $50 and $100.

A four-gallon drum is small enough to carry up stairs and onto a ladder and large enough for most cleanups. It carries the DEWALT badge and 5 peak HP for the same price as larger models from lesser brands. It ranks fifth because the capacity is limited and the listing offers no blower, attachments or filter detail.

Buy it if you need a vac that moves around job sites or between floors. Skip it if you want to clean a flooded basement.

products.name: Amazon Basics Wet Dry Shop Vacuum Cleaner, 4 Gallon, 3 HP Stainless Steel
products.verdict: A 4 gallon stainless steel vac rated 3 HP, sized for smaller garages and closets.
products.description:
The Amazon Basics shop vacuum is a four gallon wet-dry machine with a stainless steel drum and a 3 HP rating, between $50 and $100.

Stainless steel is more rigid than poly and resists dents, which suits a vac that gets knocked around. It is compact enough to store in a closet. It ranks sixth because the horsepower is the lowest of the larger group, and the price is above the Stanley's with less capacity. Features such as a blower are not listed.

Buy it if you have a smaller garage and want a steel drum. Skip it if you want more capacity for the price.
cons: Costs more than Stanley for less tank
products.skipIf: You want maximum tank per dollar.

products.name: CRAFTSMAN CMXEVBE17250 2.5 Gallon 2.5 Peak HP Wet Dry Shop Vacuum
products.verdict: A 2.5 gallon, 2.5 peak HP shop vac that is small, cheap and easy to store.
products.description:
The CRAFTSMAN CMXEVBE17250 is a 2.5 gallon wet-dry shop vacuum with a 2.5 peak HP rating, priced between $25 and $50.

It is the smallest tank in the ranking, and that is its point: a light, cheap machine for car interiors, workbench clean-ups and small spills. It will not handle a flooded basement or a pile of drywall dust, and the 2.5 gallon drum fills quickly. It ranks last on capacity but earns its place on portability and price.

Buy it if you want a compact vac for the car and the workbench. Skip it if you need to clear large messes.

methodology.title: Tank capacity
methodology.description: Tanks from 2.5 to 9 gallons were compared first, since they decide how often you must stop and empty the drum.

methodology.title: Motor claims
methodology.description: Peak horsepower figures of 2.5, 3, 4 and 5 were treated as marketing numbers, and weighed lightly against tank and filter.

methodology.title: Filtration
methodology.description: A self-cleaning filter and the presence of attachments were credited for dusty jobs and varied use.

methodology.title: Build and portability
methodology.description: Poly and stainless steel drums, portable designs and the weight of a full tank were considered.

methodology.title: Value
methodology.description: Feature depth was set against the $25 to $50, $50 to $100 and $100 to $200 brackets.

whatMatters.detail: Pick the size for your biggest regular job. 2.5 gallons suits cars and benches, 4 to 6 gallons fits most garages, and 8 to 9 gallons suits workshops and flooded basements. A bigger tank is heavier to move when it is full of water.

Peak HP is measured with no load, so it overstates real power. A 5 HP rating does not mean five times the pickup of a 1 HP unit. Use it only to compare among models, and weigh hose diameter and filter more.

Wet pickup needs a foam sleeve, and fine dust needs a cartridge or HEPA-style filter. Using the wrong one clogs fast or damages the motor. A self-cleaning filter, as on the Vacmaster, helps with dust.
A wider hose moves debris like wood chips and gravel. Attachments help with corners and upholstery. Many listings omit hose size, so check the product page or the manual.
A blower port turns the exhaust into a stream of air for clearing leaves and dust. A drain spout lets you empty liquids without lifting the drum. Both are convenient, and the DXV06P offers a blower.

cards.text: A large tank, a drain spout and a foam sleeve for wet pickup. Keep the machine away from standing water and plug it into a GFCI outlet.

faq.q: Can I use a shop vac for wet and dry messes?
faq.a: Yes, but swap the filter. Use a foam sleeve for liquid and a paper or cartridge filter for dust, and never vacuum wet with a dry filter fitted. Empty the tank after wet pickup and let it dry.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake with shop vacuums?
faq.a: Buying on horsepower. Peak HP is a no-load figure and barely predicts performance. Choose by tank size, hose and filter, and match them to your jobs.

faq.q: Is the DEWALT 9 gallon worth it over the 6 gallon?
faq.a: If you fill a drum often, yes. For ordinary garage jobs, the DXV06P offers a blower and a lower price. The larger drum matters on job sites and in workshops.
Attach the casters and wheels, fit the filter and bag if needed, and screw on the hose. Most take 10 to 15 minutes, and the main thing to get right is the correct filter.

faq.q: How do I clean the filter?
faq.a: Tap dust off outside, rinse washable filters and let them dry before reuse. A clogged filter is the most common reason for weak suction. Replace filters that are torn.

faq.q: Is it safe to use near water?
faq.a: Shop vacs are made for wet pickup, but plug them into a GFCI outlet, keep the cord away from water and never stand in a puddle while it runs. Follow the manual's guidance.

finalTake: For heavy and frequent use, the DEWALT 9 Gallon is the best wet-dry vacuum here. The DEWALT DXV06P with a blower is the best all-rounder for a garage, the Vacmaster suits dusty workshops, and the Stanley is the cheap workhorse. Choose by tank and filter, and ignore the horsepower badge.
